questions.q: What is the core difference between a standard RAG pipeline and agentic RAG?
options: Agentic RAG does not use an embedding model
In agentic RAG, retrieval is exposed as a tool the model decides whether and when to call, rather than a fixed step that always runs first
Agentic RAG skips prompt assembly entirely
Agentic RAG only works with graph databases
questions.explain: Standard RAG retrieves automatically before generation; agentic RAG lets the model itself decide whether retrieval is needed and whether to call it again.

questions.q: What does a tool definition like 'search_knowledge_base' passed to the Messages API actually contain?
options: The full text of every document in the knowledge base
The vector database's connection credentials
A name, description, and input_schema describing what the tool does and what input it expects
A pre-computed list of all possible search results
questions.explain: A tool definition tells the model what the tool is for and what input shape to provide — it does not contain the knowledge base's actual content.

questions.q: What does a 'tool_use' content block in the model's response represent?
options: The final answer to the user's question
An error returned by the vector database
A citation referencing a specific source document
A request from the model to call a specific tool with specific input, rather than a plain text answer
questions.explain: A tool_use block is the model asking the application to run a specific tool (like search_knowledge_base) with a specific input, instead of responding directly.

questions.q: Why might agentic RAG call the retrieval tool more than once for a single user question?
options: Because the Messages API requires at least two tool calls per request
Because every tool call must be repeated exactly twice for validation
Because the model can read what a first search returned, decide it doesn't fully answer a multi-part question, and issue a second, more targeted search
Because vector databases require duplicate queries to return results
questions.explain: Agentic RAG can adapt mid-conversation — retrieving again with a refined query if the first search's results don't fully answer the question.

questions.q: What is the main trade-off agentic RAG makes compared to a single-pass retrieval pipeline?
options: It trades predictability and known cost/latency for the ability to adapt its retrieval strategy mid-conversation
It trades answer accuracy for faster response times
It trades citation support for lower embedding costs
It trades chunk size flexibility for larger vector dimensionality
questions.explain: A single-pass pipeline has one predictable retrieval call; an agentic loop may call retrieval an unknown number of times, trading that predictability for adaptability on genuinely multi-step questions.
